dimensions.explanation: The selected control concerns material investment changes in the post-authorisation setting for the circular's defined UCITS funds. Management companies are addressed, but the relief attaches to scheme changes. Other funds and operator changes are outside this selected control.

UCITS funds is expressly defined. Materiality, novel or complex product features, home-jurisdiction compliance and possible local policy implications lack operational definitions in the supplied text.

The exceptions attach to approval relief for investment changes: novelty, complexity or possible local policy implications independently defeats the stated relief. The language does not support requiring all three together.

The text removes a prior-approval requirement for qualifying changes. It does not certify compliance or eliminate notification, filing, post-vetting or regulatory action. Failure to qualify for removal does not itself fully establish the underlying approval obligation.

The express date is 28 November 2025. Pre-date applications pending at transition retain existing processing. Whether this necessarily preserves a substantive prior-approval prerequisite, rather than just the handling of the application, is not fully specified.

The operative FAQs, referenced forms and checklists, home requirements and existing approval process are not supplied. The two dependency records have no source hashes or contents, and cannot be reliably mapped to particular referenced documents.

Do the FAQs impose any separate home-supervision condition beyond compliance with home-jurisdiction requirements for investment changes?

citations.quote: The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:

Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC.

readings.distinction: The text supports a clear removal-of-approval eligibility rule for changes outside the transition, rather than rival conjunctive and disjunctive exception rules. For example, an ordinary home-compliant investment-policy change in a covered Irish UCITS after the Effective Date qualifies if it has no possible local policy implications; the same change with possible local policy implications does not qualify even if it is neither novel nor complex. For an otherwise identical application received on 27 November 2025 and pending at transition, existing processing applies and this formal control gives no answer. The strongest uncertainty is whether that preserved processing also necessarily preserves the substantive approval prerequisite.

readings.statement: [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] Selected control: eligibility for removal of prior SFC approval for a material UCITS investment change outside the legacy-application transition. Within the stated scope, true means the change meets the circular's stated home-compliance condition and none of its stated exceptions applies. False means this removal is unavailable under those conditions; it does not independently establish a prohibition, non-compliance or the complete underlying approval obligation. Outside scope, the result supplies no determination. Unknown facts remain unknown.
